definitions.definition: ell=max(λ,0), regarded as a natural number (the integer-to-natural conversion λ.toNat). This definition imposes no range condition on λ.
J=Fin(ell+1), identified with the integers i satisfying 0≤i≤ell.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ x^r, with x^0=Id_V. Factorials are the usual products, with 0!=1.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ y^r, with y^0=Id_V.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ)
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is generated over ℤ by the divided powers x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r. Its action on V is generated by the operators X_r,Y_r. Operator stability under this algebra means stability under every generator.

V_K=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second factor. This is the original V(K). For any f∈End_ℤ(M), f⊗Id_K acts by u⊗a↦f(u)⊗a. The original induced x,y,h actions are the tensor extensions of their restrictions to M; h|M=(x|M)(y|M)−(y|M)(x|M).
Q=K⊗_ℤ M, with K acting on the first factor.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, A_r=X_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every X_r preserves M. In particular A_1=x|M and A_0=Id_M.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, B_r=Y_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every Y_r preserves M. In particular B_1=y|M and B_0=Id_M.

For f∈End_ℤ(M), Fext(f)=Id_K⊗f is the scalar extension obtained by the balanced tensor construction; on pure tensors Fext(f)(a⊗u)=a⊗f(u). Its additivity, multiplicativity, unitality and compatibility with integer scalars are conclusions to prove when used.

τ is the balanced tensor map specified by τ(u⊗a)=a⊗u. The scalar action on V_K is on its second factor and on Q on its first factor. Bijectivity and operator intertwining are assertions to prove, rather than part of this definition.

inputs.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.
For every abelian group M with its integer module structure, every integer basis b indexed by Fin n, and every field K, there exists a K-basis c of K⊗_ℤ M indexed by Fin n whose ith vector is 1⊗b_i.

output.statement: For every integer basis (b_i)_(i∈J) of M, the vectors 1⊗b_i form a K-basis of Q. In particular Q is finite dimensional, dim_K Q=ell+1>0, and Q is nonzero. The map τ:V_K→Q is a K-linear isomorphism, with inverse a⊗u↦u⊗a. For every f∈End_ℤ(M), τ∘(f⊗Id_K)=Fext(f)∘τ. Consequently V_K is also nonzero of K-dimension ell+1. In particular this intertwining applies to f=A_1=x|M, f=B_1=y|M, and f=h|M=A_1 B_1−B_1 A_1.

argument.text: H001 supplies an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V. Since dim_ℂ V=λ+1 and λ≥0, that basis has ell+1 elements and can be indexed by J=Fin(ell+1). Here the usual finite-basis count follows from independence and spanning in a finite-dimensional vector space. Thus at least one integer basis of M indexed by J exists.

produces.statement: There exists an integer basis of M indexed by J.

argument.text: Let b be any such integer basis. Apply E003 to M,b,K with n=ell+1. It yields a K-basis c of Q whose ith vector is 1⊗b_i.

produces.statement: There exists a K-basis c of Q indexed by J such that c_i=1⊗b_i for every i∈J.

binders.type: K-basis of Q indexed by J

argument.text: Choose c with the properties of F002. Its equality with the family (1⊗b_i) shows that this very family is a K-basis; b was arbitrary, so this holds for every integer basis of M indexed by J.

produces.statement: The vectors 1⊗b_i, i∈J, form a K-basis of Q.

argument.text: Apply E006 to the basis c to get dim_K Q=ell+1. A finite basis spans, so Q is finite dimensional. Since ell+1>0, Q is nonzero: specifically J contains index 0, and the corresponding basis vector c_0 cannot be zero by independence.

produces.statement: Q is finite dimensional, dim_K Q=ell+1>0, and Q is nonzero.

argument.text: The preceding basis assertion holds for every b, while the dimension and nonzero conclusions are independent of its choice. Existential elimination using F001 therefore gives those conclusions unconditionally under H001.

For all u∈M and a∈K, the formula τ(u⊗a)=a⊗u respects additivity and integer balance: for every z∈ℤ, (z u)⊗a and u⊗(z a) both map to a⊗(z u)=(z a)⊗u. For every t∈K, τ(u⊗(t a))=(t a)⊗u=t(a⊗u), which proves K-linearity. Define the reverse balanced map σ(a⊗u)=u⊗a for all a∈K,u∈M. The same relations prove its well-definedness and K-linearity. Both composites are identity on pure tensors, and hence everywhere, since every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus σ=τ⁻¹.

produces.statement: τ:V_K→Q is a K-linear isomorphism with inverse σ satisfying σ(a⊗u)=u⊗a for every a∈K,u∈M.

argument.text: For any f∈End_ℤ(M), both τ∘(f⊗Id_K) and Fext(f)∘τ send u⊗a to a⊗f(u). K-linearity and spanning by pure tensors prove equality. Since x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M by H001, A_1=x|M and B_1=y|M. Also h=xy−yx preserves M and h|M=A_1 B_1−B_1 A_1. Thus the equality applies to all three original induced generators. Finally, the inverse σ transports any K-basis of Q to a K-basis of V_K: linear independence and spanning follow by applying the inverse maps to linear relations and expansions. Consequently V_K has dimension ell+1 and is nonzero. Together with the universally established basis statement and F004–F005, this proves the asserted output.
